title: EGA VI. Plans, notations, problèmes ouverts : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a planning page for the projected later chapters of EGA (the material on Hilbert, Quot and Picard schemes that was to extend FGA, Exposés 221 and 232/236). It has three parts.

(1) A list of topics. Some are struck through, which probably means 'transferred elsewhere' or 'dropped'.
- Struck: a finiteness theorem for Hilbert schemes, i.e. boundedness / quasi-compactness of the components or of families with given invariants.
- Struck: Matsusaka's theorem on automorphisms of a polarized variety. The modern statement is that the automorphism group of (X, L) is of finite type, and finite in the appropriate cases. This is the Matsusaka–Mumford circle of ideas.
- Kept: 'Th. de la courbe générique [pour Picard]'. This is the classical Weil–Chow–Lang device: one studies Pic^0 (or Pic^τ) of X through the Jacobian of a generic curve section, which gives an injection or surjection between the Picard variety and the Jacobian (Albanese) of a curve. It is used to prove properness/abelianness of Pic^0 and finiteness of NS/Pic^τ.
- Struck: Hilbert schemes of a curve over S, and Picard of curves over S, with a query about 'Θ divisors'. This points to a relative theta divisor on the relative Jacobian.
- Kept: Picard of a proper non-projective k-scheme. This is the representability question settled by Murre (1964) and Oort (1962) for proper schemes over a field.
- Kept: Picard of a projective S-scheme with reducible fibres, e.g. a curve over S. This is the non-separatedness / representability problem treated later by Raynaud (1970, 'Spécialisation du foncteur de Picard'), and in the algebraic-space setting by Artin (1969).

(2) A dependency diagram of chapters or sections labelled A–L.
- Arrows: A→B; B→H; B→G; C→G; C⇢H (dashed); D→F; E→F; F→G; D→J; H→I; G→I.
- K is isolated. L sits below a horizontal rule, next to 'Appendice : Pbs ouverts'.
- So the plan ends in an appendix of open problems. The letters are not identified on this page, so the assignment of topics to letters cannot be reconstructed.

(3) Several long diagonal strokes cross the whole page. This is Grothendieck's usual way of marking a sheet as superseded or already transferred.

The next page gives the notational conventions for the functors Quot, Hilb, Div, Hom, Isom, Aut, Imm, Π_{Y/S}, Prépic and Pic, so this page sits in the 'plans' part of the dossier.
errors: No mathematical assertions are made, only topic headings and a dependency graph, so there is nothing to check for correctness.

ideas.modern_name: Boundedness / quasi-projectivity of Hilbert scheme components; finiteness of Hilbert polynomials in bounded families

ideas.what: Matsusaka's theorem on automorphisms of a polarized variety
ideas.modern_name: Aut(X,L) is a group scheme of finite type (Matsusaka–Mumford)
ideas.where_published: FGA Exposé 221 mentions Aut schemes; Matsusaka's theorem itself is not treated there in full as far as I know

ideas.what: Generic curve theorem used for the Picard scheme
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz-type comparison: Pic^0(X) and the Jacobian of a generic (complete-intersection) curve section
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in FGA 236 (TDTE VI) in the discussion of Pic^τ; unsure

ideas.what: Picard of curves over S with theta divisors
ideas.modern_name: Relative Jacobian and relative theta divisor

ideas.what: Picard scheme of a proper non-projective scheme over a field
ideas.modern_name: Representability of Pic for proper k-schemes
ideas.where_published: Posed as a problem in FGA 232/236

ideas.what: Picard of a projective S-scheme with reducible fibres
ideas.modern_name: Non-separated Picard functor, Pic as algebraic space, Néron models of Jacobians

missed.claim: The page documents that the unwritten EGA chapters on Picard were planned to include the generic-curve theorem, Picard for proper non-projective schemes, and Picard over S with reducible fibres, closing with an appendix of open problems. This is useful for the history of EGA but contains no new mathematics; every topic was later treated by Murre, Oort, Artin, Raynaud and Kleiman.
missed.quote: Picard d'un S-schéma projectif à fibres réductibles [p.ex. cas d'une courbe sur S] ... Appendice : Pbs ouverts.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only: it fills in the planned scope of EGA V/VI.

deep.surprise_reason: A table-of-contents and dependency plan for unwritten EGA chapters, mostly crossed out. Every listed topic is classical and was resolved by others in the 1960s–70s.

L stands below the horizontal rule, on the same line as 'Appendice : Pbs ouverts'; it is probably the label of that appendix.
In 'Schémas de Hilbert d'une courbe [?] sur S' the crossed-out word after 'courbe' is illegible; the whole line is struck.
